> [!WARNING]
>
> **The hostname is not `k8s.wlkr.ch`**
>
> This site is on a second domain. It needs the `wollbi.ch` listener and certificate on the apps Gateway and `wollbi.ch` in external-dns' `domainFilters`, all in the platform repository. Without them the route exists, resolves to nothing and serves no certificate.

- **A new field needs a migration.** The Postgres adapter ignores schema push in production, so a collection change that works on a laptop does nothing here until `payload migrate:create` has been run and committed in the site repository.
- **The uploads volume and the database restore together.** The uploads come back from a Velero night, the database from its WAL archive; restore the database to that night's backup time ([Point-in-time restore](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#point-in-time-restore>)), or records point at files that are gone.
- **Deleting `kv/fest-wollbi/config` logs the editors out.**

# Flowscape

[Flowscape](<https://github.com/JanWelker/flowscape>) draws the whole cluster's network traffic as one 3D scene: namespaces as platforms, workloads as lights, every conversation an arc with sparks coloured by verdict. Hubble UI shows one namespace at a time; this answers "who talks to whom across namespaces, and what would a policy have dropped" in one picture. Its upstream is the user's own repository, and it deploys as plain manifests around that image, per [Conventions → Official upstream sources only](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>).

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | [flowscape.k8s.wlkr.ch](<https://flowscape.k8s.wlkr.ch>); a [live demo](<https://janwelker.github.io/flowscape/>) with a synthetic cluster runs in the browser |
| Authentication | Authentik proxy outpost; the app has none of its own |
| Storage | None. Five minutes of counters in memory, rebuilt from Relay on every start |
| Database | None |
| Reads | Hubble Relay in `kube-system`, plaintext gRPC on the pod port |
| Files | [`flowscape/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/tree/main/flowscape>) |

## Configuration

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Plain manifests, no chart | One stateless process with one port; the [application repository](<https://github.com/JanWelker/flowscape/blob/main/deploy/README.md>) lists what any deployment needs, and that is all there is |
| The namespace enforces `restricted` | The image is distroless, runs as uid 65532, writes nothing and needs no capability, so the strictest profile costs nothing |
| `automountServiceAccountToken: false` | The flow metadata already carries namespace, workload, identity, ports and verdict; the app never talks to the API server, so it holds no token |
| `HUBBLE_RELAY_ADDR` on the Service port | Relay's Service maps 80 to the pod's 4245 and serves plaintext: the Cilium chart enables TLS only on the agent leg by default. The network policy names the pod port because policy sees the backend, not the Service |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is the hostname | The WebSocket accepts only browsers that loaded the page from `flowscape.k8s.wlkr.ch`; anything else is refused before the socket opens |
| Readiness ignores the Relay connection | The outpost turns a failing readiness probe into a 502 on the whole site. A Relay outage shows as a red status pill in the UI and `flowscape_relay_connected 0` in Prometheus instead, so the page stays up to say what is wrong |
| `revisionHistoryLimit: 2` | Superseded ReplicaSets keep their Trivy config-audit reports until garbage collection; the default keeps ten |
| `HTTPRoute` targets `authentik-server`, not the app | Every flow in the cluster, with pod names, ports and request paths, is visible in the UI; the outpost authenticates before the request reaches it. The cross-namespace `backendRef` works only because the platform's `referencegrant.yaml` names this namespace. Pointing the route at the Service instead silently removes the whole authentication layer, so it deserves a second look in review |

### Network policy

Every rule in `flowscape/networkpolicy.yaml`, and why it is there. The shape is [Conventions → Ship a `CiliumNetworkPolicy`](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#5-ship-a-ciliumnetworkpolicy>); rollout and debugging are in [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#network-policies>).

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Ingress on 8080 from the Authentik server pods only, with an L7 `http` rule | The outpost is the only path to the UI, and the WebSocket upgrade passes the proxy the same way Home Assistant's does. No `fromEntities: ingress`, so a request straight from the Gateway cannot skip the login |
| Ingress from Prometheus on 8080, `GET /metrics` only | The metrics share the port with the UI; the path match keeps the scraper away from `/api` and `/ws` |
| Egress to `hubble-relay` in `kube-system` on 4245 | The one thing the app dials. The matching ingress rule on Relay's own policy lives in the platform repository, so reading every flow in the cluster is deliberately a change on both sides |
| No `toFQDNs`, no `kube-apiserver` | Nothing outside the cluster and no API access are needed; the absence is the point |

## Usage

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Drag, scroll | Orbit and zoom; the scene auto-rotates until the first drag |
| Group by | Platforms are namespaces or cluster nodes; the switch animates the regrouping, and in node view the arcs between platforms are the traffic that crosses the WireGuard mesh |
| Node chips | Hover to highlight the workloads on that machine, click to hide them; a red dot marks a node Hubble Relay cannot reach |
| Click a light or an arc | Counters, rates over the window, ports, HTTP paths and DNS names seen at L7, drop reasons, a sparkline |
| Namespace chips | Hide a namespace; alt-click shows only that one |
| Verdict and protocol chips | Hide arcs and sparks of that kind |
| Window slider | 10 s to 5 min; rates and the sparkline follow |
| `space`, `f` | Pause, fit the ring into the view |

`world` is split by the name the Hubble DNS proxy resolved, so an arc to `github.com` and one to `smtp.mailbox.org` are distinct. `kube-apiserver` and `ingress` sit on the outer ring; the Gateway's Envoy is `ingress`, which is why user traffic arrives from there. The cluster's nodes sit at the back of that ring under their own names: a flow's reporting agent places the pod on its node, and the `host` and `remote-node` identities resolve to the machine once one flow there has shown its address as `host`. Nothing is read from the API server for this.

Without the cluster, the same binary runs on a laptop with `--demo` or replays a capture; the [README](<https://github.com/JanWelker/flowscape#run-it>) has both.

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n flowscape get pods
kubectl -n flowscape port-forward deploy/flowscape 8080:8080 &
curl -s localhost:8080/api/status
```

The image is distroless, so there is no shell to `exec` into, and the route answers with Authentik's login, so the status endpoint is read through a port-forward.

`status.relay` should read `connected` with an empty `unavailable` list. In Grafana, `flowscape_relay_connected` and `flowscape_relay_unavailable_nodes` say the same over time, and `rate(flowscape_flows_received_total[5m])` should sit in the hundreds per second.

## Pitfalls

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Amber means audited, not blocked**
>
> With `policyAuditMode` on, a policy that would deny a flow logs an `AUDIT` verdict and lets it through. Amber arcs are exactly the conversations that break the day audit mode is switched off — see [Security Policies → Rollout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#rollout>). Red arcs are real drops.

- **It is live, not history.** Relay's buffer is minutes deep and the app keeps five minutes; the record of what a policy refused last week is in Loki, via the Hubble export the platform tails.
- **The status pill, not the pod, reports a Relay outage.** Readiness stays green on purpose (see Configuration), so `kubectl get pods` looks fine while the scene is empty. Check `/api/status` or the metric.
- **Sparks are a sample.** The server sends at most 200 flow events per second per browser and the browser adds synthetic ones in proportion to the rate; the counters in the panel are exact, the particles are not.

# Home Assistant

[Home Assistant](<https://www.home-assistant.io/>) runs the house. Upstream publishes no Helm chart and the community ones are repackagers, so `home-assistant/` is plain manifests around the official image: `deployment.yaml`, `service.yaml`, `pvc.yaml`, `configmap.yaml`, `httproute.yaml`, `database.yaml` with `backup.yaml`, `networkpolicy.yaml` and `namespace.yaml`, per [Conventions → Official upstream sources only](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>).

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | [home.k8s.wlkr.ch](<https://home.k8s.wlkr.ch>) |
| Authentication | Authentik proxy outpost, in front of Home Assistant's own login |
| Storage | `rook-ceph-block` PVC for `/config` |
| Database | CloudNativePG `Cluster` `home-assistant-db`, for the recorder |
| Files | [`home-assistant/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/tree/main/home-assistant>) |

## State

| State | Where | Rebuildable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Registries, users, tokens, integration config (`/config/.storage`) | The `home-assistant-config` PVC | **No.** Losing it means re-pairing every device; the nightly [Velero snapshot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/>) is the only copy |
| History and long-term statistics | PostgreSQL, via CloudNativePG | From its WAL archive, to any point inside its retention window |
| `configuration.yaml` | A ConfigMap, in Git | Yes |

## Configuration

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Plain manifests, no chart | Home Assistant is one stateful process with one volume and one port; a Deployment is less work than auditing a third-party chart on every bump |
| `strategy: Recreate`, one replica | The `/config` PVC is `ReadWriteOnce`, and two Home Assistant processes against one `/config` corrupt the `.storage` registries |
| `revisionHistoryLimit: 2` | Superseded ReplicaSets keep their Trivy config-audit reports until they are garbage-collected; the Kubernetes default keeps ten |
| Root with every capability dropped but `NET_BIND_SERVICE`, no API token; the namespace enforces `baseline` | The image runs as root under s6 and writes `/config`, and upstream does not support running it otherwise, so `runAsNonRoot` and a read-only root do not apply. Root owns everything it touches; `deployment.yaml` keeps `NET_BIND_SERVICE`, which no port it opens needs, 1900 and 8123 being above 1024. `baseline` forbids adding `NET_RAW`, so DHCP discovery joins the [discovery that does not work here](<#pitfalls>) anyway. Nothing in the pod talks to the API server, so the `default` ServiceAccount's token stays unmounted, per [Default ServiceAccount tokens](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#default-serviceaccount-tokens>) |
| An init container from the same image seeds `/config` on every start | `configuration.yaml` includes `automations.yaml`, `scripts.yaml` and `scenes.yaml` so the UI editors can save; on a fresh volume they do not exist and Home Assistant fails to start rather than create them. Same image as the main container because Renovate updates every occurrence in one pull request, so the two cannot drift |
| A long `startupProbe` | Home Assistant loads every integration before it serves anything, minutes rather than seconds on a cold start with a populated registry. The startup probe buys that time without making the liveness probe useless afterwards |
| Recorder on CloudNativePG, not SQLite | SQLite's locking on a network block device is the usual cause of a Home Assistant that feels slow. `purge_keep_days` is raised because the default of 10 is shorter than the moment you look for a graph. See [the contract](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#the-contract>) |
| `secrets.yaml` written by the init container on every start | Home Assistant has no `!env_var` tag, so the database URL reaches `configuration.yaml` through `!secret`, from CloudNativePG's Secret, which the operator rotates. The value is written through `json.dumps` so it is valid YAML whatever the generated password contains. Anything added to that file by hand is lost at the next restart; secrets belong in [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/>) |
| `use_x_forwarded_for` with the pod CIDR in `trusted_proxies` | Requests arrive from Cilium's Envoy and the outpost. Without it every request has one source address, so the ban list and rate limiting count the household as one user |
| `HTTPRoute` targets `authentik-server`, not the app | The outpost authenticates and forwards to `home-assistant.home-assistant.svc:8123`. Home Assistant is the one proxied app with a login of its own, so browser users log in twice: defence in depth, not SSO. The cross-namespace `backendRef` works only because the platform's `referencegrant.yaml` names this namespace. Pointing the route at the Home Assistant Service instead silently removes the whole authentication layer, so it deserves a second look in review |
| `frontend.extra_module_url`, with `umami.js` from the ConfigMap mounted under `/config/www` | The Umami snippet. The frontend loads the URL through `import()`, and the tracker reads its website ID off its own `<script>` tag, so the module appends that tag rather than being it. See [Umami → Usage](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/umami/#usage>) |

### Network policy

The rules in `home-assistant/networkpolicy.yaml`, and why each is there. The shape is [Conventions → Ship a `CiliumNetworkPolicy`](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#5-ship-a-ciliumnetworkpolicy>); rollout and debugging are in [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#network-policies>).

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Ingress from the namespace, from `host` and `remote-node`; egress to the namespace | The rules every policy carries: [What every policy contains](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#what-every-policy-contains>) |
| Ingress on 8123 from the Authentik server pods only | The outpost is the only path to the UI. No `fromEntities: ingress`, so a request straight from the Gateway cannot skip it. Nothing else in the cluster has a reason to connect: this namespace holds a long-lived token for every device in the house. With the rule missing, the hostname answers with a gateway error after a successful Authentik login |
| Ingress from Prometheus on 9187, `GET /metrics` only | The database's metrics; a week of Hubble records showed no other request |
| Ingress from `cnpg-system` on 8000 | The operator polls the instance manager there; without the rule the `Cluster` never goes Healthy and the sync deadlocks. See [Sync stuck on the database](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#sync-stuck-on-the-database>) |
| Egress to `*.home-assistant.io` | The alerts feed and version data. An integration that talks to a device or a cloud is a line here first |
| Egress to the multicast and limited-broadcast ranges on 5353 and 1900 | The mDNS and SSDP discovery sockets keep sending, and the overlay carries it nowhere. Allowed only so it does not fill the drop log |
| Egress from the database pod to `kube-apiserver` | The instance manager reports its status there; its liveness check fails otherwise. The object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's `cnpg-backups` policy, see [CloudNativePG → Backups](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#backups>) |

## Usage

The ConfigMap is mounted over `/config/configuration.yaml`, so Git is the source of truth and the UI cannot edit it; everything Home Assistant writes for itself stays on the PVC underneath. The file is read once at startup, so a merged change does nothing until the pod restarts:

```bash
kubectl -n home-assistant rollout restart deploy/home-assistant
```

The UI's own restart button does the same from inside.

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n home-assistant get pods,pvc
kubectl -n home-assistant get cluster home-assistant-db
```

The database should report `Cluster in healthy state`. A pod stuck in `Init` is waiting on it: the init container cannot write `secrets.yaml` until CloudNativePG has produced the Secret.

## Pitfalls

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The API is not behind Authentik**
>
> `/api/`, `/auth/token` and the external-auth callback are exempt on the provider, so Home Assistant's own accounts guard them and revoking an Authentik account does not revoke a Home Assistant token: do that under Settings → People. See [Authentik → Pitfalls](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/#pitfalls>).

- **No local device discovery.** mDNS and SSDP need host networking, which needs a `privileged` namespace. Add devices by IP, or through an integration that does not rely on broadcast, and add the address to the egress policy.
- **No USB devices.** A Zigbee or Z-Wave stick pins the pod to one machine. Use a network-attached coordinator instead.
- **The cluster is now a dependency of the lights.** A Ceph rebalance that pauses I/O pauses Home Assistant with it.

# Knead Time

[Knead Time](<https://kneadtime.pizza>) is a static pizza-dough calculator on GitHub Pages. Its step reminders cannot come from the page — iOS wakes a web app's service worker only for a server-sent push — so this is the one server it has: a small FastAPI service that holds a phone's push subscription and the times of its hands-on steps, and sends a Web Push notification when each comes due. The source and the image live in the [knead-time](<https://github.com/JanWelker/knead-time/tree/main/push>) repository, so like Flowscape it deploys as plain manifests around our own image, per [Conventions → Official upstream sources only](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>).

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | [kneadtime.k8s.wlkr.ch](<https://kneadtime.k8s.wlkr.ch/v1/vapid>), an API under `/v1`; the app that calls it is [kneadtime.pizza](<https://kneadtime.pizza>) |
| Authentication | None. Browsers on kneadtime.pizza call it directly; CORS admits that origin only |
| Storage | None on the pod |
| Database | CloudNativePG `Cluster` `kneadtime-db` |
| Dials | The browsers' push services, over HTTPS |
| Files | [`kneadtime/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/tree/main/kneadtime>) |

## State

| State | Where | Rebuildable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Push subscriptions and the reminders queued for them | PostgreSQL, via CloudNativePG | Only by every phone tapping **Remind me** again; a lost database means one missed bake, not a lost account |
| The VAPID private key | OpenBao `kv/kneadtime/config`, through an ExternalSecret | No — rotating it retires every subscription taken with the old key |

## Configuration

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Plain manifests, no chart | One process, one port, one database; the [service README](<https://github.com/JanWelker/knead-time/blob/main/push/README.md>) lists the environment and that is all there is |
| The namespace enforces `restricted` | The image runs as uid 65532, writes nothing and needs no capability; CloudNativePG's pods declare restricted-compliant contexts of their own |
| One replica, the default `RollingUpdate` | The dispatcher that sends due reminders runs inside the process and claims due rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so the two copies that overlap during a rollout never send the same reminder; nothing on the pod needs a `Recreate` gap |
| A `Cluster`, not SQLite on a PVC | [Conventions → PostgreSQL is always a CloudNativePG Cluster](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#3-postgresql-is-always-a-cloudnativepg-cluster>); `DATABASE_URL` is the `uri` key the operator writes to `kneadtime-db-app` |
| `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` from OpenBao | A P-256 key in PEM, generated by `make bao-secrets` because a `Password` generator cannot produce one, which is why [rule 7](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#7-real-secrets-come-from-openbao>)'s `PushSecret` path does not apply; the service derives the public half at startup and serves it, so the static site carries no key |
| `VAPID_SUBJECT` is the site URL | The contact a push service may use; a URL rather than a mailbox keeps an address out of a manifest |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is the site | Only pages loaded from `kneadtime.pizza` may call the API from a browser; PR previews of the app live under the same origin |
| `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is the pod CIDR | Envoy is the only thing that reaches the pod, and it appends the client's address to `X-Forwarded-For`; uvicorn trusts that header from the pod network only, so the service's per-address rate limit ([`ratelimit.py`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/knead-time/blob/main/push/kneadtime_push/ratelimit.py>)) counts the phone, not the Gateway |
| `HTTPRoute` targets the app's own Service | Nobody logs in — browsers call the API on behalf of a phone that already gave its subscription. The Dependency-Track shape, not the Flowscape one |
| `HTTPRoute` matches `/v1` only | The app serves its API, its probes and `/metrics` on one port; the browser calls only `/v1/vapid` and `/v1/schedules` (`src/lib/push/api.ts` in the app repository), and the counters describe usage that is nobody else's business |
| `revisionHistoryLimit: 2` | Superseded ReplicaSets keep their Trivy config-audit reports until garbage collection; the default keeps ten |

### Network policy

The rules in `kneadtime/networkpolicy.yaml`, and why each is there. The shape is [Conventions → Ship a `CiliumNetworkPolicy`](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#5-ship-a-ciliumnetworkpolicy>).

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Ingress from the namespace, from `host` and `remote-node`; egress to the namespace | The rules every policy carries: [What every policy contains](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#what-every-policy-contains>) |
| Ingress on 8080 from `ingress` | The Gateway reaches the pod directly; there is no outpost to skip |
| Ingress from Prometheus on 8080 and 9187, `GET /metrics` only | The app's counters and the database's exporter |
| Ingress from `cnpg-system` on 8000 | The operator reads the instance manager's status |
| Egress to the four push-service names on 443 | Apple, Google, Mozilla and Microsoft are where subscriptions live. The service refuses any other host at request time, so this list and the code's allow-list are one decision taken twice |
| The instance pods reach `kube-apiserver` | The CloudNativePG instance manager reports its status there. The object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's `cnpg-backups` policy, see [CloudNativePG → Backups](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#backups>) |

### Secrets

`kv/kneadtime/config` holds one key, `vapid-private-key`, written by `make bao-secrets` in the platform repository. Overwriting it is gated behind a typed confirmation there: the push services answer 401 or 403 for every subscription taken with the old key, the service deletes them, and every phone has to opt in again.

## Usage

Nothing to operate by hand. A phone with the app on its Home Screen taps **Remind me on this device** in the plan's menu; the receipt notification that arrives at once is the end-to-end check.

```bash
curl -s https://kneadtime.k8s.wlkr.ch/v1/vapid     # the public key, from outside the LAN
```

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n kneadtime get pods,cluster,externalsecret,httproute
kubectl -n kneadtime port-forward svc/kneadtime 8080:80 &
curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep kneadtime_push
```

`kneadtime_push_sent_total` moves when a reminder goes out; `gone_total` counts subscriptions the push services refused.

## Pitfalls

- **The image has to be public on GHCR.** The cluster has no pull secret for `ghcr.io/janwelker`; a version published while the package was private stays `ImagePullBackOff` until the package's visibility is changed.
- **`readyz` is the database.** A pod that is up but not ready is a database that is not reachable; check the `Cluster` before the pod.
- **Nothing here sends on its own schedule.** A reminder that did not arrive is either a subscription the push service retired (`gone_total` rose, the phone has to opt in again) or a phone whose Home Screen icon was removed, which drops the subscription on the device side.

# OpenCloud

[OpenCloud](<https://opencloud.eu/>) is the household's file sync and share: one Go binary, no database, with desktop, iOS and Android clients. Upstream publishes no open Helm chart, so `opencloud/` is plain manifests around the official image: `deployment.yaml`, `service.yaml`, `pvc.yaml`, `httproute.yaml`, `servicemonitor.yaml`, `secrets.yaml`, `networkpolicy.yaml`, `namespace.yaml` and two ConfigMaps, `csp.yaml` and `authentik-blueprint.yaml`, per [Conventions → Official upstream sources only](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>).

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | [cloud.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch](<https://cloud.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch>), LAN and VPN only |
| Authentication | Authentik OIDC for every client; the built-in identity provider does not run |
| Storage | `rook-ceph-block` PVC for `/var/lib/opencloud`, the PosixFS driver |
| Database | None; metadata lives in extended attributes and the embedded NATS store |
| Secrets | `kv/opencloud/config` in OpenBao, generated once |
| Files | [`opencloud/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/tree/main/opencloud>) |

## Storage

PosixFS keeps the files on the volume in the tree the user sees, with the metadata in xattrs, which ext4 provides, and versions, trash and the search index beside them. One volume holds the whole instance, so the nightly [Velero snapshot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/>) is a complete copy, and a restore is readable with `ls`. The driver's non-collaborative mode requires that nothing else writes to the tree, which a single Deployment on a `ReadWriteOnce` volume guarantees.

The alternative, blobs in an S3 bucket with metadata on a volume, splits one instance across two backup mechanisms, one of which does not exist for buckets here, and upstream documents no migration into or out of it.

Upstream's backup guidance is to stop the instance first. The RBD snapshot is crash-consistent instead: metadata is written per operation on the same filesystem, and the nightly [Velero](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/>) run sees no sync traffic. The search index is rebuilt if it disagrees after a restore; nothing is lost.

## Configuration

The values in `opencloud/deployment.yaml` that are not self-explanatory:

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `opencloudeu/opencloud-rolling`, not the production `opencloudeu/opencloud` | Rolling ships every three weeks on a current Alpine; the production line gets a release about every six months, and its image carried a fixable critical in an Alpine package that the [image-scan gate](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>) refuses. Move to the production line at a release that passes the gate. Either way a major bump waits for a human |
| `args: ["server"]`, no `init` | `opencloud init` only writes random secrets and IDs into `opencloud.yaml`. Every one of them arrives as an environment variable from `opencloud-env` instead, so `/etc/opencloud` is an emptyDir and the pod carries nothing a backup would have to protect |
| `strategy: Recreate`, one replica | The volume is `ReadWriteOnce`, and PosixFS in non-collaborative mode tolerates one writer |
| `runAsUser: 1000`, `fsGroup: 1000`, read-only root, the namespace enforces `restricted` | The image runs as that user and writes only under `/var/lib/opencloud`, `/etc/opencloud` and `/tmp`, the last two emptyDirs |
| `OC_EXCLUDE_RUN_SERVICES=idp` | Authentik is the identity provider; the built-in one would be a second login |
| `OC_OIDC_ISSUER=https://auth.k8s.wlkr.ch/` | The four Authentik providers run in global issuer mode, whose issuer is the bare hostname; see [OIDC](<#oidc>) |
| `PROXY_CSP_CONFIG_FILE_LOCATION`, the policy in `opencloud/csp.yaml` | The default Content-Security-Policy allows connections and frames to the server itself only, so the browser refuses the discovery, token and silent-renew requests to an external IdP and the page spins forever. The file adds `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` to `connect-src` and `frame-src`; OpenCloud merges it into the default rather than replacing it, so the default's `update.opencloud.eu` and GitHub app-store hosts stay in the browser policy. They matter only to a browser, the update check is off, and the server itself reaches neither |
| `PROXY_OIDC_REWRITE_WELLKNOWN` | The desktop and mobile clients discover the identity provider through the server's own `/.well-known/openid-configuration` |
| `PROXY_OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_VERIFY_METHOD=jwt` | Authentik's access tokens are JWTs, so the server checks signature and issuer itself instead of calling userinfo on every request |
| `PROXY_OIDC_AUDIENCES`, the four client IDs | Authentik writes the client ID into `aud`, so the server accepts only tokens minted for one of its own clients, not any token from the same issuer. Without the list the proxy logs at every start that audience validation is off |
| `PROXY_AUTOPROVISION_ACCOUNTS`, with `sub` as the username | Accounts are created in the built-in IDM on first login and keyed on the `sub` claim, which never changes, per [Conventions → Authentication](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#6-authentication-is-authentiks-not-the-applications>). Upstream's own autoprovisioning example does the same. Users see display names, never this value |
| `GRAPH_USERNAME_MATCH=none` | Authentik's `sub` is a SHA-256 hex string, and the default rule refuses a username that starts with a digit: `Invalid username`, and the first login ends in a 400 |
| `FRONTEND_READONLY_USER_ATTRIBUTES` | Name and mail come from Authentik on every login, so the profile page must not offer to edit them |
| `PROXY_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_DRIVER=oidc` on the `groups` claim, `GRAPH_ASSIGN_DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=false` | The role comes from Authentik group membership, and a user in neither group gets no role and no access; see [Usage](<#usage>) |
| `STORAGE_USERS_ID_CACHE_STORE=nats-js-kv` | PosixFS requires the NATS key-value store for its id cache; the embedded NATS provides it |
| `FRONTEND_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false` | The web frontend's version check is the one outbound call the server makes on its own. Nothing phones home, the same rule as every platform component |
| `PROXY_DEBUG_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9205` | Every service in the binary has a debug port; the proxy's carries the request metrics, the health endpoints and the one `ServiceMonitor` |
| `HTTPRoute` on `infra-gateway`, not `apps-gateway` | Only `apps-gateway` gets a public DNS record. Phones sync on the LAN and the VPN; moving to the public gateway is one route change |

### OIDC

OpenCloud's web, desktop, iOS and Android clients are four OIDC clients with IDs fixed by the clients (`web`, `OpenCloudDesktop`, `OpenCloudIOS`, `OpenCloudAndroid`), all public, authorization code with PKCE, so `opencloud/authentik-blueprint.yaml` holds four providers and four applications. Only the web one is visible in the Authentik library; the native ones carry `blank://blank` as their launch URL.

The server and the native clients verify every token against the one issuer the server advertises, and Authentik derives a provider's issuer from its application slug. All four providers therefore use `issuer_mode: global`, and the platform rewrites `/.well-known/openid-configuration` on `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` to the `opencloud` application's document; see [One issuer for OpenCloud](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/#one-issuer-for-opencloud>).

The desktop client redirects to a loopback address with a random port, so its redirect URI is a regular expression; the mobile ones are custom-scheme URLs the apps register. There are no client secrets, so nothing lands in OpenBao for Authentik's side, and the platform repository only mounts the blueprint.

### Secrets

`secrets.yaml` generates what `opencloud init` would: a `Password` generator for the JWT, transfer, URL-signing and service-account secrets, the machine-auth and system-user API keys and the IDM service passwords, which the `users`, `groups`, `auth-basic` and `graph` services also receive as their LDAP bind passwords, and one `UUID` generator per ID, because a `UUID` generator yields one value and a `PushSecret` reads one generator. Each `PushSecret` writes its keys into `kv/opencloud/config` once; the `ExternalSecret` templates them into `opencloud-env` under the environment variable names. Losing the OpenBao path and regenerating is a new instance: the JWT secret signs the internal tokens and the IDs name the storage mount and the system user, so the data on the volume would no longer match.

`idm-admin-password` is the built-in IDM's `admin` account, which the first start creates. With the IdP excluded nothing presents a login form for it, so there is no local break-glass account here, not even the one [rule 6](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#6-authentication-is-authentiks-not-the-applications>) allows: Authentik is the only way in.

### Network policy

The rules in `opencloud/networkpolicy.yaml`, and why each is there. The shape is [Conventions → Ship a `CiliumNetworkPolicy`](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#5-ship-a-ciliumnetworkpolicy>).

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Ingress from the namespace, from `host` and `remote-node`; egress to the namespace | The rules every policy carries: [What every policy contains](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#what-every-policy-contains>) |
| Ingress from `ingress` on 9200 | The Gateway reaches the server directly; OpenCloud handles its own login, and the desktop and mobile clients arrive the same way |
| Ingress from Prometheus on 9205, `GET /metrics` only | The proxy's metrics; the health endpoints on the same port are the kubelet's, covered by `host` and `remote-node` |
| Egress from the server to the Authentik server pods on 9000 | Discovery, the signing keys and the token endpoint go to `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch`, which resolves to the Gateway's own address, private but `world` to Cilium. The Gateway's Envoy then checks this policy against the Authentik pod it picks and answers 403 itself when that pod is not listed, so both the name and the pod are allowed |
| Egress from the server to `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` on 443 | The other half of the same path. Hubble records one dropped SYN to this name at each pod start: the first packet after a fresh DNS answer races the FQDN policy update and the retransmit passes, the [known artefact](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#network-policies>), not a missing rule |

No app store, no update check, no mail, no object store: the search index and NATS run inside the process.

## Usage

Membership in one of two Authentik groups is an account:

| Group | OpenCloud role |
| --- | --- |
| `opencloudAdmin` | Administrator |
| `opencloudUser` | User |

A user in neither group can log in to Authentik but is refused by OpenCloud with no role assigned. The groups also appear as groups inside OpenCloud, because autoprovisioning mirrors the `groups` claim.

Clients: the [desktop client](<https://github.com/opencloud-eu/desktop/releases>) for macOS 13 and later, Windows and Linux, the iOS app from the App Store and the Android app from Google Play or F-Droid. Each takes the server URL and opens Authentik in the browser.

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n opencloud get pods,pvc,externalsecret,pushsecret
curl -s https://cloud.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq -r .issuer
```

The pod is `Running`, every `PushSecret` and the `ExternalSecret` are `Ready`, and the issuer printed is `https://auth.k8s.wlkr.ch/`. After a first start, the `idm.boltdb` on the volume is larger than the 32 KiB of an empty Bolt file; see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>).

```bash
kubectl -n opencloud exec deploy/opencloud -- ls -l /var/lib/opencloud/idm/
```

## Pitfalls

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `ExternalSecret` stays `SecretSyncedError` on the first sync | The `PushSecret`s and the `ExternalSecret` are in different waves but OpenBao is written asynchronously; the retry covers it within minutes |
| The web page shows the loading animation forever, the console reports a Content-Security-Policy violation for `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` | The served policy is the default, not `csp.yaml`: the ConfigMap or `PROXY_CSP_CONFIG_FILE_LOCATION` is missing, or the mount path differs from the variable |
| Login succeeds in Authentik, OpenCloud answers 403 | The user is in neither group, or the issuer in the token differs from `OC_OIDC_ISSUER`: a provider without `issuer_mode: global` |
| The desktop client's login tab never returns | The loopback redirect did not match the regular expression; the port is random and the path may be empty |
| Prometheus shows the target down | The policy allows `GET /metrics` only; any other path on 9205 from Prometheus is refused |
| Login ends on "Not logged in"; the log shows `failed to add user` with `LDAP Result Code 49` from `graph` and `not found` from `idm` | The IDM database under `idm/` on the volume is a bare Bolt file: a first pod that died during the bootstrap, as in the row below, left it created but without the service users, and every later start sees the file and skips the bootstrap. Remove the `idm` directory ([Recovery](<#recovery>)); the next start bootstraps it. Only safe while no account exists yet, which is the case when this symptom appears |
| The pod exits with `error parsing mapping JSON: unexpected end of JSON input` from the `search` service | The Bleve index under `search/` on the volume was created by a pod that died before writing the mapping, which happens when another service fails on the same first start. Remove the `search` directory ([Recovery](<#recovery>)); the index is rebuilt from the files on the next start |

## Recovery

### Removing a directory from the volume

For the two first-start failures above. The volume is `ReadWriteOnce` and stays attached to the node of the crashing pod, so the debug pod goes on that node; scaling the Deployment to zero first does not hold, self-heal restores the replica within a minute.

1. Start a debug pod beside the crashing one, on its node and from its image, with the `restricted` context the namespace enforces:

   ```bash
   NODE=$(kubectl -n opencloud get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=opencloud -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.nodeName}')
   IMAGE=$(kubectl -n opencloud get deploy opencloud -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
   kubectl -n opencloud apply -f - <<EOF
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: opencloud-debug
   spec:
     nodeName: $NODE
     restartPolicy: Never
     automountServiceAccountToken: false
     securityContext:
       runAsNonRoot: true
       runAsUser: 1000
       runAsGroup: 1000
       fsGroup: 1000
       seccompProfile:
         type: RuntimeDefault
     containers:
       - name: shell
         image: $IMAGE
         command: ["sleep", "3600"]
         securityContext:
           allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
           capabilities:
             drop: ["ALL"]
         volumeMounts:
           - name: data
             mountPath: /var/lib/opencloud
     volumes:
       - name: data
         persistentVolumeClaim:
           claimName: opencloud-data
   EOF
   ```
2. Remove the directory, `idm` or `search`:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n opencloud exec opencloud-debug -- rm -r /var/lib/opencloud/search
   ```
3. Delete the debug pod; the container's next restart recreates what was removed:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n opencloud delete pod opencloud-debug
   ```

# Shot Timer bridge

The bridge is the always-on half of the Shot Timer iPhone app. iOS will not let an app hold the La Marzocco cloud websocket open in the background, so this one process watches the machine, tracks each shot, looks up the machine's exact extraction time afterwards, keeps the shot history in SQLite, and starts and updates the phone's Live Activity through APNs. The phone and watch apps call its small HTTP API. The source, the image and the chart live in [somuch-cloud/extractor.cafe](<https://github.com/somuch-cloud/extractor.cafe/tree/main/deploy>); the chart is published to `ghcr.io/somuch-cloud/charts`, per [Conventions → Official upstream sources only](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>).

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | [shot.k8s.wlkr.ch](<https://shot.k8s.wlkr.ch/healthz>), an API for the iPhone and watch apps |
| Authentication | The bridge's own bearer key; the apps cannot go through Authentik |
| Storage | PVC `shot-bridge`, SQLite and the La Marzocco installation key |
| Database | CloudNativePG `Cluster` `shot-bridge-db`, a primary and a streaming replica |
| Dials | `lion.lamarzocco.io`, APNs |
| Files | [`shot-bridge/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/tree/main/shot-bridge>) |

## State

| State | Where | Rebuildable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shot history, registered phones, default dose, coffees, reference shots | PostgreSQL, the CloudNativePG `Cluster` `shot-bridge-db` (`database.yaml`) | History from its WAL archive, to any point inside its retention window; phones re-register on their next launch |
| La Marzocco installation key | `installation_key.json` on the PVC | Yes, the bridge registers a new one on start |
| Account credentials and the APNs key | OpenBao `kv/shot-bridge/accounts` | Re-typed from the accounts |
| API key | OpenBao `kv/shot-bridge/config`, generated | Yes, then entered again in the iPhone app |

## Configuration

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Own chart, values in `application.yaml` | The chart ships the Deployment, PVC, Service, `HTTPRoute` and the bridge's `CiliumNetworkPolicy`; this directory adds the namespace, the secrets and the namespace's default-deny policies in `networkpolicy.yaml`, which are what police the database pods |
| One replica, `Recreate` | One cloud websocket; two copies would double every push |
| `database.existingSecret: shot-bridge-db-app` | The bridge reads `DATABASE_URL` from the Secret CloudNativePG writes for `shot-bridge-db` (`uri` key); without it the chart falls back to the SQLite file on the PVC. The PVC stays for the La Marzocco installation key |
| `Cluster` `shot-bridge-db`, two instances, 1Gi | A few rows a day, but the phones log every shot as it happens; a replica turns a drain or a node loss into a failover of seconds instead of a restart. `enablePDB: false` still, so the drain triggers that failover rather than hanging, and a topology spread keeps the two on different nodes. WAL and a nightly base backup through `backup.yaml` |
| `HTTPRoute` targets the bridge's Service | The phone sends `Authorization: Bearer`; an Authentik outpost in front would answer the app with a login page |
| Probes are TCP | `/healthz` returns 503 whenever the machine is off, and the apps still need the history then |
| `apns.env: sandbox` | The iPhone app is installed from Xcode with development signing; TestFlight builds need `production` |
| `apns.bundleId` and `apns.teamId` | Must match the app's bundle ID and team, or APNs rejects every push |
| `lm.serial` | The machine to watch; the chart requires it |
| `admin.enabled: true` | The [admin UI](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/extractor-admin/index.md>)'s read-only token, and its pods let in on 8080 |
| `timeZone: Europe/Zurich` | The bridge dates a bag's opening by the day of its first shot; the image runs in UTC otherwise, so a shot before 01:00 or 02:00 would land on the day before |

### Network policy

The chart's `CiliumNetworkPolicy` selects the bridge's pod; the `default-ingress`, `default-egress` and `database` policies in `networkpolicy.yaml` select the whole namespace, so the database pods are default-deny too. All at sync wave `-2`. The shape is [Conventions → Ship a `CiliumNetworkPolicy`](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#5-ship-a-ciliumnetworkpolicy>).

| File | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chart | Ingress on 8080 from `ingress` and `host` | The Gateway, and the kubelet's probes; the chart admits `host` alone where the namespace policies below admit `remote-node` too |
| Chart | Ingress on 8080 from the admin UI's pods | `admin.enabled`; the [admin UI](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/extractor-admin/index.md>) reads with its token |
| Chart | Egress to `lion.lamarzocco.io` on 443 | The La Marzocco REST API and websocket |
| Chart | Egress to the Kaffeemacher shop and `cdn.shopify.com` on 443 | The coffee catalog and the bag photos |
| Chart | Egress to the four APNs names on 443, 2195 and 2196 | Pushes and broadcasts on 443; channel management on 2195 (sandbox) and 2196 (production) |
| Chart | Egress to the namespace on `database.port` | The database's `-rw` Service, rendered because `database.existingSecret` is set |
| Chart | Egress to `kube-dns` on 53 | The chart's own DNS rule; the platform's cluster-wide rule grants the same, so it adds nothing here |
| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Ingress from the namespace, from `host` and `remote-node`; egress to the namespace | The rules every policy carries, here for the database pods too: [What every policy contains](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#what-every-policy-contains>); the replica streams from the primary through them |
| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Ingress from Prometheus on 9187, `GET /metrics` only | The database's exporter, through its `PodMonitor`; the bridge exposes no metrics |
| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Ingress from `cnpg-system` on 8000 | The operator reads the instance manager's status; without it the `Cluster` never goes Healthy |
| `networkpolicy.yaml` | The instance pods reach `kube-apiserver` | The CloudNativePG instance manager reports its status there; the object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's `cnpg-backups` policy, see [CloudNativePG → Backups](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#backups>) |

### Secrets

| Path | Keys | Written by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kv/shot-bridge/accounts` | `lm-username`, `lm-password`, `apns-key-id`, `apns-key-p8` | `make bao-secrets` in the platform repository |
| `kv/shot-bridge/config` | `api-key`, `admin-read-key` (the [admin UI](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/extractor-admin/index.md>)'s read-only token, which it reads from [a copy](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/extractor-admin/#copying-the-read-key>)) | The `PushSecret` in `secrets.yaml` |

The accounts path holds values from outside the cluster, so it is its own path: a `bao kv put` replaces a path wholesale. `make bao-secrets` asks for the La Marzocco login, then the APNs key ID and the path to the `.p8` file; Enter leaves the APNs half empty until the key exists.

## Usage

Read the API key and enter it with `https://shot.k8s.wlkr.ch` in the iPhone app's setup screen; **Test** shows the machine's state.

```bash
kubectl -n shot-bridge get secret shot-bridge -o jsonpath='{.data.BRIDGE_API_KEY}' | base64 -d
```

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n shot-bridge get pods,externalsecret,httproute
curl -s https://shot.k8s.wlkr.ch/healthz    # 200 while the machine is reachable, 503 while it is off
kubectl -n shot-bridge logs deploy/shot-bridge
```

## Pitfalls

- **The image and chart have to be public on GHCR.** The cluster has no pull secret for `ghcr.io/somuch-cloud`, and ArgoCD has no credentials for the chart registry.
- **The sync stops at wave `-1` until `kv/shot-bridge/accounts` exists.** The `ExternalSecret` fails on a missing path, so the Deployment is never created; run `make bao-secrets`.
- **The pod crash-loops while the APNs keys are empty.** The bridge exits on a missing variable rather than starting half-configured.
- **Rotating `kv/shot-bridge/config` changes both keys.** The `PushSecret` writes `IfNotExists`, so rotating is [deleting the path](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#rotating-a-credential>). The phone is logged out: enter the new API key in the app's setup screen, the watch receives it from the phone. The [admin UI](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/extractor-admin/index.md>) reads a hand copy of `admin-read-key` and answers 403 until it is [copied again](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/extractor-admin/#copying-the-read-key>).

# Umami

[Umami](<https://umami.is/>) counts the visits to every site: the two documentation sites, the GitHub Pages projects and Home Assistant. It sets no cookie and stores no address, so the sites need no consent banner. Upstream publishes an image and no chart, so `umami/` is plain manifests around the official image: `deployment.yaml`, `service.yaml`, `pdb.yaml`, `httproute.yaml`, `database.yaml` with `backup.yaml`, `secrets.yaml`, `networkpolicy.yaml` and `namespace.yaml`, per [Conventions → Official upstream sources only](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#2-official-upstream-sources-only>).

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | [analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch](<https://analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch>) |
| Authentication | Authentik proxy outpost, in front of Umami's own login; `/script.js` and `/api/send` pass through |
| Storage | None outside the database |
| Database | CloudNativePG `Cluster` `umami-db` |
| Secrets | `kv/umami/config` in OpenBao |
| Files | [`umami/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/tree/main/umami>) |

## Configuration

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Plain manifests, no chart | One stateless process with one port and one database; the community charts are repackagers |
| The namespace enforces `restricted` | The image runs as uid 1001, needs no capability, and writes only Next.js' cache, which is an `emptyDir` next to `/tmp` |
| `automountServiceAccountToken: false` | Umami never talks to the API server |
| `DATABASE_URL` from `umami-db-app`, key `uri` | Umami wants one connection string, and CloudNativePG assembles it; see [the contract](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#the-contract>) |
| `APP_SECRET` and `TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY` from OpenBao | The first signs every dashboard session and the second encrypts TOTP secrets; both must survive a rebuild, so the `PushSecret` writes each to OpenBao once and a rebuilt cluster reads the same value back. See [Secrets](<#secrets>) |
| `DISABLE_UPDATES`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `PRIVATE_MODE` | No phone-home: no version check, no usage report, no favicon fetch for each tracked site. The egress policy allows nothing outside the cluster, so these are what keep the log free of drops |
| Two replicas, a hard spread across nodes, a `PodDisruptionBudget` | Nothing lives on the pod and the sessions are JWTs signed by the shared `APP_SECRET`, so a second instance keeps the tracker up through a Kured drain and an image bump; the migrations at start take a Postgres advisory lock, so two pods starting together do not race |
| Probes on `/api/heartbeat`, a long `startupProbe` | The first start runs the Prisma migrations before the server answers |
| `revisionHistoryLimit: 2` | Superseded ReplicaSets keep their Trivy config-audit reports until garbage collection; the default keeps ten |
| `HTTPRoute` targets `authentik-server`, not the app | The outpost authenticates and forwards to `umami.umami.svc:3000`. The provider's `skip_path_regex`, in the platform repository, exempts exactly `/script.js` and `/api/send`: the tracker every visitor loads and the endpoint it posts to. Everything else, the dashboard and the rest of the API, is behind the login. The cross-namespace `backendRef` works only because the platform's `referencegrant.yaml` names this namespace; pointing the route at the Umami Service removes the authentication layer, so it deserves a second look in review |
| No `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | The Gateway's Envoy appends the visitor to `X-Forwarded-For` and the outpost passes it on; Umami reads that header by default. Only the country is stored, from the bundled GeoLite database, never the address |

### Network policy

The rules in `umami/networkpolicy.yaml`, and why each is there. The shape is [Conventions → Ship a `CiliumNetworkPolicy`](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#5-ship-a-ciliumnetworkpolicy>); rollout and debugging are in [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#network-policies>).

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Ingress from the namespace, from `host` and `remote-node`; egress to the namespace | The rules every policy carries: [What every policy contains](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#what-every-policy-contains>) |
| Ingress on 3000 from the Authentik server pods only | The outpost proxies the tracker paths as well as the dashboard, so the Gateway never talks to the pod. No `fromEntities: ingress`, so a request straight from the Gateway cannot skip the login |
| Ingress from Prometheus on 9187, `GET /metrics` only | The database's metrics. Umami itself exposes none |
| Ingress from `cnpg-system` on 8000 | The operator polls the instance manager there; without the rule the `Cluster` never goes Healthy and the sync deadlocks. See [Sync stuck on the database](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#sync-stuck-on-the-database>) |
| Egress to the namespace only | The database. With the three phone-home switches off, nothing else is dialled |
| Egress from the database pod to `kube-apiserver` | The instance manager reports its status there; its liveness check fails otherwise. The object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's `cnpg-backups` policy, see [CloudNativePG → Backups](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#backups>) |

### Secrets

`kv/umami/config` holds two values, 64 hex characters each as Umami documents them, written once by the `PushSecret` in `secrets.yaml` and never overwritten — see [Generated secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#generated-secrets>).

| Key | Read as |
| --- | --- |
| `app-secret` | `APP_SECRET`: signs the dashboard sessions |
| `two-factor-encryption-key` | `TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY`: encrypts TOTP secrets at rest |

The `ExternalSecret` sits at sync wave `-1`, with the database and ahead of the Deployment that reads it, and keeps its Secret when deleted (`deletionPolicy: Retain`). The database password is not here; CloudNativePG generates it and nothing outside the cluster needs it.

## Usage

### First login

Umami creates `admin` with the password `umami` on its first start. Change it under Profile before adding a website; it is the only account, and the only credential Umami keeps that OpenBao does not.

### Adding a site

1. Settings → Websites → Add website: a name and the hostname. The website ID it shows is not a secret; it goes into Git with the snippet.
2. Put the snippet in the site's `<head>`, with `data-domains` set to the hostname it should report from:

   ```html
   <script defer src="https://analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch/script.js"
     data-website-id="<id>" data-domains="<hostname>"></script>
   ```

`data-domains` is what keeps a local `zensical serve` or `npm run dev` out of the numbers: the tracker checks the page's hostname before it sends anything. A PR preview under the production hostname is not excluded and counts as a page there.

Where the snippet lives per site:

| Site | Where |
| --- | --- |
| This site and the [platform documentation](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/>) | `overrides/partials/integrations/analytics/custom.html`, wired by `[project.extra.analytics] provider = "custom"` in `zensical.toml` |
| A SvelteKit or Vite site on GitHub Pages | `src/app.html` or `index.html` |
| [Home Assistant](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/home-assistant/index.md>) | `frontend.extra_module_url` in `configuration.yaml`, pointing at a module in the ConfigMap that appends the `<script>` tag; a module is loaded through `import()`, which is not how the tracker expects to be run |

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n umami get pods
kubectl -n umami get cluster umami-db
curl -sI https://analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch/script.js | head -1
```

The database should report `Cluster in healthy state` and the script should answer `200` without a redirect to `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch`. The dashboard's Realtime view is the end-to-end check: open one of the sites and the visit appears within seconds.

## Pitfalls

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Two logins, and the tracker paths behind neither**
>
> Browser users authenticate twice, and `/script.js` and `/api/send` are behind neither login; the collect endpoint accepts nothing but page views and events for a known website ID. See [Authentik → Pitfalls](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/#pitfalls>).

- **A visit shows the cluster's country, or none.** Umami takes the visitor from `X-Forwarded-For`. If every visit resolves to the same place, the header is not reaching the pod: see [Behind the Gateway](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#behind-the-gateway>).
- **Deleting `kv/umami/config` logs everyone out.** The `PushSecret` writes both keys anew: a rotated `APP_SECRET` invalidates every session and a rotated 2FA key every second factor.
- **`data-domains` is the only guard against noise.** A snippet without it reports from every copy of the site: a laptop, a preview, a fork.
